title.en: The Manifest Book and God's signs

essay.en: The surah opens with the disconnected letters Ha, Meem and an oath by the Manifest Book. God has made it 'an Arabic Quran so that you may exercise your reason'; yet al-Mizan notes that in its own station in the Mother Book, with God, the Book lies beyond the reach of created minds, and was dressed in Arabic only so that reason might find its way to it [1]. Al-Tibyan reads the Mother Book as the Preserved Tablet, in which God has written all that will be until the Day of Resurrection [6]. Then comes a rebuke: 'Shall We keep back the Reminder from you and disregard you because you are an unrestrained lot?' Majma al-Bayan reads this as a question that answers itself; God will not hold back the revelation and neglect them for their excess in disbelief [3]. To steady the Prophet against his people's mockery, the passage recalls that every earlier nation derided its prophet, and that God destroyed peoples far stronger than the Quraysh [4]. The argument then rests on the idolaters' own words. Asked who created the heavens and the earth, they can only answer that 'the All-mighty, the All-knowing' did, which exposes their ignorance, since they still worship others beside Him and deny His power to raise the dead [4]. The passage then lists what is in truth His management of their lives: the earth spread as a cradle, its paths, and rain sent down in measure, neither too much to ruin nor too little to harm, reviving a dead land as He will raise them from their graves [5]. He made the pairs, and the ships and cattle they ride, and taught them to remember His blessing and glorify Him when they are settled on them, owning that they return to their Lord. It closes on their ingratitude: they assign Him 'offspring from among His servants,' calling the angels His daughters, a claim al-Mizan calls impossible, for a part implies composition in the One who is undivided [2]. Man, the passage ends, is a manifest ingrate.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله (عليه السلام)، و قد تلا هذه الآية: وَإِنَّهُ فِيۤ أُمِّ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ، قال: علي بن أبي طالب (عليه السلام).
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja'far, from al-Rida, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Having recited 'and it is sublime and wise with Us in the Mother Book,' he said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هو أمير المؤمنين (صلوات الله عليه) و معرفته، و الدليل على أنه أمير المؤمنين قوله تعالى: وَإِنَّهُ فِيۤ أُمِّ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: [The straight path of al-Fatiha] is Amir al-Muminin and knowing him; and the proof that it is Amir al-Muminin is God's words, 'and it is sublime and wise with Us in the Mother Book.'

note.en: Even idolaters concede that God alone is Creator; narrations trace this admission to the innate knowledge of God set in every person from birth [57].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فَطَرَهُمْ عَلَى الْمَعْرِفَةِ بِهِ … كُلُّ مَوْلُودٍ يُولَدُ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ يَعْنِي الْمَعْرِفَةَ بِأَنَّ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ خَالِقُهُ كَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالأرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ الله.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, from Abu Jafar

text.en: God created them upon the fitra, the recognition that He is their Creator. The Prophet said, 'Every newborn is born upon the fitra,' meaning the recognition that God is his Creator; and so is His saying, 'if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say: God.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ذكر النعمة أن تقول: الحمد لله الذي هدانا للإسلام، و علمنا القرآن، و من علينا بمحمد (صلى الله عليه و آله)، و تقول بعده: سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا إلى آخر الآية.
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, by his chain, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Remembering the blessing is to say, 'Praise be to God who guided us to Islam, taught us the Quran, and favored us with Muhammad,' and then to say, 'Glory be to Him who has disposed this for us,' to the end of the verse.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: و استويت على راحلتك، فقل: سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَـٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ، فإنه ما ركب أحد ظهرا قط فقال هذا و سقط، إلا لم يصبه كسر و لا وبال و لا وهن.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat

text.en: When you set out by land and are settled on your mount, say, 'Glory be to Him who has disposed this for us, and we were no match for it, and indeed we shall return to our Lord.' No one mounts and says this and then falls but suffers no fracture, harm, or injury.

perspectives.en: Verse 4 calls the Book 'sublime and wise' in the Mother Book. Sunni commentators such as al-Tabari take these words as attributes of the Quran itself: it is of high rank and firmly decided, its verses made sound [25]. Shia narrations read them differently: al-Burhan gathers reports from the Imams identifying the 'sublime' one with Amir al-Muminin Ali, whose place in the Book is marked again in al-Fatiha's 'Guide us on the straight path' [18]. The two traditions agree the verse exalts what is with God; they differ on whether that is the scripture or Ali.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فمفاد الآية أن الكتاب بحسب موطنه الذي له في نفسه أمر وراء الفكر أجنبي عن العقول البشرية وإنما جعله الله قرآناً عربياً وألبسه هذا اللباس رجاء أن يستأنس به عقول الناس فيعقلوه

sources.gloss: The Book, in the station it has in itself, is a matter beyond thought, foreign to human minds; God only made it an Arabic Quran and clothed it in this garb so that people's minds might grow familiar with it and reason.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وإنما عبّر عن الولد بالجزء للإِشارة إلى استحالة دعواهم

sources.gloss: The offspring is expressed as a 'portion' only to point to the impossibility of their claim.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أفنمسك عن إنزال القرآن ونهملكم فلا نعرّفكم ما يجب عليكم من أجل أنكم أسرفتم في كفركم وهذا استفهام إنكار ومعناه إنّا لا نفعل ذلك

sources.gloss: Shall We hold back sending down the Quran and neglect you, not teaching you what you owe, because you have gone to excess in your disbelief? This is a rhetorical denial, meaning: We will not do that.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وهذا إخبار عن غاية جهلهم إذ اعترفوا بأنّ الله خلق السموات والأرض ثم عبدوا معه غيره وأنكروا قدرته على البعث

sources.gloss: This tells of the utmost of their ignorance: they admitted that God created the heavens and the earth, then worshipped others alongside Him and denied His power over resurrection.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي بقدر الحاجة لا زائداً عليها فيفسد ولا ناقصاً عنها فيضرّ ولا ينفع وفي ذلك دلالة على أنّه واقع من قادر مختار قد قدّره على ما تقتضيه الحكمة

sources.gloss: That is, in the measure of need, neither more so that it would spoil, nor less so that it would harm and not benefit; a sign that it comes from a powerful, choosing agent who has measured it as wisdom requires.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: في أم الكتاب لدنيا يعنى اللوح المحفوظ الذي كتب الله فيه ما يكون إلى يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: 'In the Mother Book with Us' means the Preserved Tablet, in which God has written what will be until the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و الدليل على أنه أمير المؤمنين قوله تعالى: وَإِنَّهُ فِيۤ أُمِّ ٱلْكِتَابِ لَدَيْنَا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ

sources.gloss: The proof that it is Amir al-Muminin is God's words: 'and it is sublime and wise with Us in the Mother Book.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ذكر النعمة أن تقول: الحمد لله الذي هدانا للإسلام، و علمنا القرآن، و من علينا بمحمد (صلى الله عليه و آله)

sources.gloss: Remembering the blessing is to say: Praise be to God who guided us to Islam, taught us the Quran, and favored us with Muhammad.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: لعليّ: يقول: لذو علوّ ورفعة، حكيم: قد أحكمت آياته، ثم فصلت فهو ذو حكمة

sources.gloss: 'Sublime' means: possessed of loftiness and elevation; 'wise' means: its verses have been made firm and then set forth in detail, so it is possessed of wisdom.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: كُلُّ مَوْلُودٍ يُولَدُ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ يَعْنِي الْمَعْرِفَةَ بِأَنَّ الله عَزَّ وَجَلَّ خَالِقُهُ كَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالأرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ الله

sources.gloss: Every newborn is born upon the fitra, that is, the recognition that God is his Creator; and so is His saying: 'if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say: God.'

essay.en:
The passage drives a single charge home: the Meccans insult God by giving Him what they cannot bear for themselves. They assign Him daughters while keeping sons for their own line, yet when one of them is told he has a daughter his face darkens and he chokes with rage. The Quran turns their scorn back on them - would they ascribe to God a child 'brought up amid ornaments' who cannot make its case in a dispute? Commentators read this as the very daughters they scorned, too weak to argue their own side [2], though Abu Zayd, in a reading al-Tibyan judges weaker, took it to mean the idols [4].

The core error is calling the angels female. The Quran answers that these are the 'servants of the All-beneficent,' a title that does not fit females, and asks whether the pagans stood witness at their creation; since such knowledge could come only from seeing it, and they were not present, their testimony will be written down and they will answer for it [1]. Then comes their excuse: 'Had the All-beneficent wished, we would not have worshipped them.' Tabatabai calls this a specious argument that confuses God's creative will with His legislative will, taking the one for the other [1]. Nor can they point to any earlier scripture that grants the claim [1].

What remains is imitation. They found their fathers on a creed and walk in their tracks, and the Quran replies that every warner before Muhammad met the same answer from a town's affluent ones, for ease and luxury turn people from inquiry to blind following [1]. The warner presses: even if I bring better guidance than your fathers had? They refuse outright. So God took vengeance, and the closing call to observe the deniers' fate warns the Prophet's own people [1] while showing that the good end belongs to those who hold the truth [3].

note.en: Al-Qummi glosses 'ornaments' as gold and relates that Pharaoh flung this taunt at Moses, whom God had let appear robed in gold, mocking him as one who could not speak plainly [7].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kadhim
narrations.arabic: علينا نزل قبل الناس، و لنا فسر قبل أن يفسر في الناس … فنحن حكماء الله في أرضه، و شهداؤه على خلقه، و هو قوله تبارك و تعالى: { سَتُكْتَبُ شَهَادَتُهُمْ وَيُسْأَلُونَ } ، فالشهادة لنا، و المسألة للمشهود عليه
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far, from Abu al-Hasan

text.en: It was revealed upon us before the people, and interpreted for us before it was interpreted among them. We are God's judges on His earth and His witnesses over His creation. That is His word, 'Their testimony will be written down and they shall be questioned': the testimony is ours, the questioning for the one testified against.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ذكر أبو جعفر (عليه السلام) الكتاب الذي تعاقدوا عليه في الكعبة، و أشهدوا فيه، و ختموا عليه بخواتيمهم، فقال: يا [أبا] محمد، إن الله أخبر نبيه بما يصنعونه قبل أن يكتبوه، و أنزل الله فيه كتابا … نعم، ألم تسمع قول الله تعالى: { سَتُكْتَبُ شَهَادَتُهُمْ وَيُسْأَلُونَ }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Maliki, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Khalaf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Imam al-Baqir recalled the pact they sealed in the Kaba with their seals, and said: God told His prophet what they would do before they wrote it, and sent down a scripture about it. I asked, A scripture? He said: Yes; have you not heard, 'Their testimony will be written down and they shall be questioned'?

perspectives.en: Verse 20's excuse - 'Had the All-beneficent wished, we would not have worshipped them' - divides the traditions on divine will. Tusi reads it as a refutation of the Determinists: God does not will the repugnant acts of His servants, so their attempt to shelter their idolatry behind His will is false [4]. Qurtubi, reading as an Ash'ari, treats the sentence as a word of truth put to a false use, since everything does happen by God's will; the pagans' fault lay not in affirming that will but in the conclusion they drew from it [28].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وقوله { ما لهم بذلك من علم } أي هو منهم قول مبني على الجهل فإنه مغالطة خلطوا فيها بين الإِرادة التكوينية والإِرادة التشريعية وأخذ الأولى مكان الثانية

sources.gloss: His words 'they have no knowledge of that' mean their claim rests on ignorance, for it is a fallacy in which they confused the creative will with the legislative will, taking the first in place of the second.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال قتادة: قلّما تتكلم امرأة بحجّتها إلا تكلّمت بالحجة عليها أي لا يمكنها أن تبين الحجة عند الخصومة لضعفها وسفهها

sources.gloss: Qatada said: rarely does a woman speak in her own defense without speaking against herself; in a dispute she cannot make her argument plain, owing to her weakness and folly.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وفي هذا إشارة إلى أنّ العاقبة المحمودة تكون لأهل الحق والمصدّقين لرسل الله

sources.gloss: In this is a sign that the praiseworthy end belongs to the people of truth and to those who affirm God's messengers.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ففي ذلك إبطال مذهب المجبرة فى ان الله تعالى يريد القبيح من افعال العباد

sources.gloss: In this is the refutation of the Determinists' doctrine that God wills the repugnant among the acts of His servants.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال إن موسى عليه السلام أعطاه الله من القوة أن أرى فرعون صورته على فرس من ذهب رطب عليه ثياب من ذهب رطب، فقال فرعون أو من ينشؤا في الحلية أي: ينشؤا بالذهب

sources.gloss: He said: Moses was given by God the power to show Pharaoh his form on a horse of moist gold, wearing garments of moist gold, so Pharaoh said, 'One who is brought up amid ornaments,' that is, brought up in gold.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فنحن حكماء الله في أرضه، و شهداؤه على خلقه، و هو قوله تبارك و تعالى: { سَتُكْتَبُ شَهَادَتُهُمْ وَيُسْأَلُونَ } ، فالشهادة لنا، و المسألة للمشهود عليه

sources.gloss: We are God's judges on His earth and His witnesses over His creation, and that is His word 'Their testimony will be written down and they shall be questioned': the testimony is ours, and the questioning is for the one testified against.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وهذا منهم كلمة حق أريد بها باطل. وكل شيء بإرادة الله

sources.gloss: This from them is a word of truth by which falsehood is intended; and everything is by God's will.

title.en: Abraham's word and the world's wares

essay.en: The passage turns from Quraysh's clinging to their fathers' ways to Abraham, the very ancestor they claim. He repudiates every object his father and people worship, keeping only the One who originated him and who, he trusts, will guide him. Commentators place his story here as the argument of a man who reasoned his way to God while his people only imitated their elders [2]. He made this a lasting word among his posterity, so that they may come back. The commentators read it as the word of tawhid, 'There is no god but God,' which never dies out among Abraham's descendants [4], while narrations read the enduring word as the Imamah in al-Husayn's line [13]. Rather than return, these people and their fathers were left to enjoy the world until the truth, the Quran, and a manifest apostle, Muhammad, reached them [4]; and when it came they called it magic. They objected that such a book should have been sent down on a great man of the two cities, Mecca and Taif, meaning great in wealth and standing [3]. Commentators name al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Urwa ibn Masud, though al-Mizan treats these as the exegetes' own identifications [1]. God answers that they do not apportion His mercy, which is prophethood. He apportions their very livelihood, raising some above others so that people take one another into service [3]; and His mercy outweighs all they amass. Were it not that everyone would rally to disbelief out of love for the world, He would give those who reject Him silver roofs, stairways, doors, couches, and gold, for such things weigh nothing with Him [5]. All of it is nothing but the wares of the life of this world; the Hereafter, near your Lord, is for the Godwary [5].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألت أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) عن قول الله عز و جل: { وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ } ، قال: هي الإمامة، جعلها الله عز و جل في عقب الحسين (عليه السلام)، باقية إلى يوم القيامة
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani, from Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakhai, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Basir

text.en: Abu Basir asked about the verse 'He made it a lasting word among his posterity.' He said: 'It is the Imamah. God placed it in the posterity of al-Husayn, remaining until the Day of Resurrection.'

narrations.speaker: The Prophet
narrations.arabic: سألت رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) عن قوله عز و جل: { وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ } ، قال: جعل الأئمة في عقب الحسين، يخرج من صلبه تسعة من الأئمة، و منهم مهدي هذه الامة
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ubaydillah al-Jawhari, from Abd al-Samad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mukram, from Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi, from Abu al-Zinad Abdullah ibn Dhakwan, from his father, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayra

text.en: Abu Hurayra asked the Prophet about 'He made it a lasting word among his posterity.' He said: 'He placed the Imams in the posterity of al-Husayn; from his loins will come nine Imams, and among them is the Mahdi of this community.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: أنه عروة بن مسعود الثقفي، و كان عاقلا لبيبا، و هو الذي أنزل الله تعالى فيه: { وَقَالُواْ لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ }
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Imam al-Sadiq said: 'It is Urwa ibn Masud al-Thaqafi, who was sensible and shrewd. It is about him that God revealed, "Why was not this Quran sent down to some great man from the two cities?"'

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: سألت علي بن الحسين (عليه السلام) عن قول الله عز و جل: { وَلَوْلاَ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً } ، قال: عنى بذلك أمة محمد أن يكونوا على دين واحد كفارا كلهم … و لو فعل ذلك بأمة محمد (صلى الله عليه و آله) لحزن المؤمنون و غمهم ذلك، و لم يناكحوهم و لم يوارثوهم
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from his father, from Sad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib al-Asadi, from his father, from Said ibn al-Musayyab

text.en: Said ibn al-Musayyab asked Ali ibn al-Husayn about 'Were it not that mankind would be one community.' He said: 'By this He meant the community of Muhammad, that they be of one religion, all disbelievers. Had He done so, the believers would grieve, and would neither marry them nor inherit from them.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فقال الصادق عليه السلام: لو فعل الله ذلك لما آمن أحد ولكنه جعل في المؤمنين أغنياء وفي الكافرين فقراء وجعل في الكافرين أغنياء وفي المؤمنين فقراء ثم امتحنهم بالأمر والنهي والصبر والرضى

text.en: Imam al-Sadiq said: 'Had God done that, no one would have believed. But He placed among the believers rich and poor, and among the disbelievers rich and poor, then tested them with command and prohibition, with patience and contentment.'

perspectives.en: On the enduring word left in Abraham's line, both traditions largely agree it is the word of tawhid, 'There is no god but God,' which never dies out among his descendants [25]. Shia narrations carry it further: al-Sadiq and other Imams identify the lasting word as the Imamah, placed in the posterity of al-Husayn until the Day of Resurrection [13]. The readings are not opposed, since guidance is the thread both follow. Notably, al-Suddi, cited by al-Tabari, glosses 'his posterity' itself as the family of Muhammad [20].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والحق أن ذلك من تطبيق المفسرين وإنما قالوا ما قالوا على الإِبهام

sources.gloss: The truth is that this is the commentators' own application; they said what they said only in indefinite terms.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقيل الكلمة الباقية في عقبه هي الإمامة إلى يوم الدين عن أبي عبد الله ع

sources.gloss: It is said the lasting word in his posterity is the Imamah until the Day of Religion, reported from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { أهم يقسمون رحمة ربّك } يعني النبوّة بين الخلق

sources.gloss: 'Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?' means prophethood among creation.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قوله: لا إله إلا الله لم يزل فى ذريته من يقولها

sources.gloss: the statement 'There is no god but God'; there never ceased to be in his progeny someone who says it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: اخبر تعالى عن هوان الدنيا عليه وقلة مقدارها عنده

sources.gloss: God announced the world's lowliness before Him and its slight worth in His sight.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فقال الصادق عليه السلام: لو فعل الله ذلك لما آمن أحد ولكنه جعل في المؤمنين أغنياء وفي الكافرين فقراء وجعل في الكافرين أغنياء وفي المؤمنين فقراء ثم امتحنهم بالأمر والنهي والصبر والرضى

sources.gloss: al-Sadiq said: Had God done that, no one would have believed; rather He placed among the believers rich and poor, and among the disbelievers rich and poor, then tested them with command and prohibition, patience and contentment.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال: هي الإمامة، جعلها الله عز و جل في عقب الحسين (عليه السلام)، باقية إلى يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: He said: It is the Imamah; God placed it in the posterity of al-Husayn, remaining until the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أنه عروة بن مسعود الثقفي، و كان عاقلا لبيبا، و هو الذي أنزل الله تعالى فيه: { وَقَالُواْ لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ }

sources.gloss: It is Urwa ibn Masud al-Thaqafi, who was sensible and shrewd; it is about him that God revealed, 'Why was not this Quran sent down to some great man from the two cities?'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عنى بذلك أمة محمد أن يكونوا على دين واحد كفارا كلهم

sources.gloss: By that He meant the community of Muhammad, that they be of one religion, all disbelievers.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: عن السديّ فِي عَقِبِهِ قال: في عقب إبراهيم آل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

sources.gloss: from al-Suddi, on 'in his posterity': in Abraham's posterity, the family of Muhammad.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: وهي لا إله إلا الله، أي جعلها دائمة في ذريته

sources.gloss: and it is 'There is no god but God'; that is, He made it enduring in his progeny.

essay.en: The surah has just weighed the gold and silver of this world and found it a passing thing; now it turns to the person who lets that world blind him to God. Whoever turns a blind eye to the remembrance of the All-beneficent has a devil assigned as his inseparable companion, and al-Mizan reads this feigned blindness as what fastens such devil-companions upon a person, clinging to him and leading him astray until they reach the punishment of the hereafter together [1]. The commentators read the verb either as deliberately turning away or as going blind to the remembrance [2]. These companions bar their charges from the way, while the misled still imagine themselves rightly guided. That partnership runs on until the resurrection, when the man wishes the distance of the two easts, that is, of east and west, lay between himself and his companion, and cries out what an evil companion he was [4]. He is told the wish is useless: since both did wrong, both will share the punishment. God then consoles His Prophet, who cannot make the deaf hear or guide the blind; the choice was never in his hands. He is promised that vengeance will fall on them whether He takes the Prophet away first or shows him the punishment in his lifetime, and the commentators read 'take you away' as either death or removal from among them [5]. The Prophet is told to hold fast to what has been revealed, for it is a straight path and a true religion [3]. That revelation is a reminder for him and for his people, and they will be questioned about it. Finally he is told to ask the messengers sent before him whether God ever set up gods to be worshipped besides the All-beneficent, a question whose answer, the single message of every prophet, is that He did not. The passage returns the surah's argument to where it started: the ornaments of the world are nothing beside the one call that all revelation carries.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله تبارك وتعالى إذا أراد بعبد خيرا نكت في قلبه نكتة من نور وفتح مسامع قلبه ووكل به ملكا يسدده، وإذا أراد بعبد سوءا نكت في قلبه نكتة سوداء وسد مسامع قلبه ووكل به شيطانا يضله
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abd Allah

text.en: If God intends good for a servant, He places a spot of light in his heart, opens the hearing of his heart, and assigns an angel to steady him. If He intends ill for a servant, He places a black spot in his heart, closes the hearing of his heart, and assigns a devil to lead him astray.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: من تصدّى بالاثم اعشى عن ذكر الله تعالى ومن ترك الأخذ عمّن امره الله بطاعته قيّض له شيطان فهو له قرين

text.en: Whoever gives himself over to sin is blinded to the remembrance of God. And whoever refuses to take from the one whom God commanded him to obey has a devil assigned to him as his companion.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نزلت هاتان الآيتان هكذا … يعني فلاناً وفلاناً يقول احدهما لصاحبه حين يراه … فقال الله لنبيّه صلّى الله عليه وآله قل لفلان وفلان واتباعهما لن ينفعكم اليوم اذ ظلمتم آل محمد صلوات الله عليهم حقّهم انّكم في العذاب مشتركون

text.en: These two verses were revealed thus: 'When he comes to Us' means so-and-so and so-and-so, one saying to the other when he sees him. God told His Prophet: say to them and their followers, since you wronged the family of Muhammad of their right, you will share in the punishment.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فإما نذهبن بك يا محمد من مكة إلى المدينة فإنا رادوك إليها ومنتقمون منهم بعلي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Abu Abd Allah

text.en: 'Whether We take you away' - O Muhammad, from Mecca to Medina - for We shall bring you back to it and take vengeance on them through Ali ibn Abi Talib.

narrations.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: لا ألفينّكم ترجعون بعدي كفاراً يضرب بعضكم رقاب بعض وأيم الله لئن فعلتموها لتعرفنّني في الكتيبة التي تضاربكم … أو علي أو علي … فأنزل الله على أثر ذلك فإمّا نذهبنّ بك فإنّا منهم منتقمون بعلي بن أبي طالب
narrations.chain: Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari

text.en: Let me not find you turning back after me as unbelievers, striking one another's necks. By God, if you do, you will know me in the squadron that fights you. Then he said, 'Or Ali, or Ali.' We saw Jibril nudge him, and God sent down, 'Whether We take you away, We will take vengeance on them' - through Ali.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: أوحى الله إلى نبيه … إنك على ولاية علي، و علي هو الصراط المستقيم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb, from Khalid ibn Mad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: God revealed to His Prophet: you are upon the wilaya of Ali, and Ali is the straight path.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: الذكر القرآن ونحن قومه ونحن المسئولون
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abd Allah

text.en: The reminder is the Quran, and we are his people, and we are the ones who will be questioned.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فرسول الله … الذكر وأهل بيته … المسئولون وهم أهل الذكر
narrations.chain: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abd Allah

text.en: The Messenger of God is the reminder, and his household are the ones who will be questioned, and they are the people of the reminder.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فكان من الآيات التي أراها الله محمداً صلى الله عليه وآله حين أسرى به إلى بيت المقدس أن حشر الله الأولين والآخرين من النبيين والمرسلين … ثم تقدم محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وصلى بالقوم فأنزل الله عليه وسئل من أرسلنا من قبلك من رسلنا
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu al-Rabi'

text.en: Among the signs God showed Muhammad when He took him by night to Jerusalem was that He gathered the first and last of the prophets and messengers; then Muhammad went forward and led them in prayer. Then God sent down, 'Ask those of Our messengers We sent before you.'

perspectives.en: On 'We will take vengeance on them' (verses 41 to 42), the commentators divide. The Sunni majority, whose view Tabari judges soundest, read the threat as aimed at the Quraysh idolaters [23], which Ibn Abbas and most commentators say God showed the Prophet at Badr [30]; Ibn Kathir adds that God did not take His Messenger until He comforted his eye with victory over his enemies [26]. The Shia narrations instead read the vengeance as taken through Ali ibn Abi Talib once the Prophet, taken from Mecca to Medina, is brought back to Mecca [8], and, one report says, on the day of Basra [14].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: تعاميهم عن ذكر الله يورثهم ملازمة قرناء الشياطين فيلازمونهم مضلّين لهم حتى يردوا عذاب الآخرة معهم

sources.gloss: Their feigned blindness to God's remembrance brings upon them the constant company of devil-companions, who cling to them and lead them astray until they arrive together at the punishment of the hereafter.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { ومن يعش عن ذكر الرحمن } أي يعرض عنه … وقيل: معناه ومن يعم عنه

sources.gloss: 'Whoever turns a blind eye to the remembrance of the All-beneficent' means whoever turns away from it; and it is said it means whoever goes blind to it.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { فاستمسك بالذي أوحي إليك } من القرآن … { إنك على صراط مستقيم } أي على دين حقّ وصواب وهو دين الإسلام

sources.gloss: Hold fast to what was revealed to you, namely the Quran; 'you are on a straight path' means on a true and correct religion, which is the religion of Islam.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: أنه عنى المشرق والمغرب الا انه غلب احدهما

sources.gloss: that he meant the east and the west, except that the name of one of the two was made to predominate.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: فيكون إذهابه به إخراجه من بين الكفار. وقال قوم: إنما أراد إذهابه بالموت

sources.gloss: so 'taking him away' would be his removal from among the unbelievers; and some said it means his being taken away by death.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فإما نذهبن بك يا محمد من مكة إلى المدينة فإنا رادوك إليها ومنتقمون منهم بعلي بن أبي طالب

sources.gloss: 'Whether We take you away' - O Muhammad, from Mecca to Medina - for We shall return you to it and take vengeance on them through Ali ibn Abi Talib.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فكان من الآيات التي أراها الله محمداً … حين أسرى به إلى بيت المقدس أن حشر الله الأولين والآخرين من النبيين والمرسلين … ثم تقدم محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وصلى بالقوم

sources.gloss: Among the signs God showed Muhammad when He took him by night to Jerusalem was that God gathered the first and last of the prophets and messengers; then Muhammad went forward and led them in prayer.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال الله: انتقم بعلي … يوم البصرة، و هو الذي وعد الله رسوله

sources.gloss: God said: I take vengeance through Ali on the day of Basra, and that is what God promised His Messenger.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: أوحى الله إلى نبيه … إنك على ولاية علي، و علي هو الصراط المستقيم

sources.gloss: God revealed to His Prophet: you are upon the guardianship of Ali, and Ali is the straight path.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: من تصدّى بالاثم اعشى عن ذكر الله تعالى ومن ترك الأخذ عمّن امره الله بطاعته قيّض له شيطان فهو له قرين

sources.gloss: Whoever gives himself over to sin is blinded to the remembrance of God; and whoever refuses to take from the one whom God commanded him to obey has a devil assigned to him as his companion.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: نزلت هاتان الآيتان هكذا … قل لفلان وفلان واتباعهما لن ينفعكم اليوم اذ ظلمتم آل محمد صلوات الله عليهم حقّهم انّكم في العذاب مشتركون

sources.gloss: These two verses were revealed thus: say to them and their followers, it will not benefit you today, since you wronged the family of Muhammad of their right, that you share in the punishment.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: وهذا القول الثاني أولى التأويلين في ذلك بالصواب وذلك أن ذلك في سياق خبر الله عن المشركين فلأن يكون ذلك تهديداً لهم أولى

sources.gloss: This second view is the sounder of the two interpretations, because the passage comes in the context of God's account of the idolaters, so its being a threat to them is more fitting.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: ولم يقبض الله تعالى رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أقر عينه من أعدائه

sources.gloss: God did not take His Messenger until He comforted his eye with victory over his enemies.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: قال ابن عباس: قد أراه الله ذلك يوم بدر وهو قول أكثر المفسرين

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas said: God showed him that on the day of Badr, and it is the view of most of the commentators.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: إذا أراد بعبد خيرا نكت في قلبه نكتة من نور … وإذا أراد بعبد سوءا نكت في قلبه نكتة سوداء وسد مسامع قلبه ووكل به شيطانا يضله

sources.gloss: If He intends good for a servant, He places a spot of light in his heart; and if He intends ill for a servant, He places a black spot in his heart, closes the hearing of his heart, and assigns a devil to lead him astray.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: الذكر القرآن ونحن قومه ونحن المسئولون

sources.gloss: The reminder is the Quran, and we are his people, and we are the ones who will be questioned.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: فرسول الله … الذكر وأهل بيته … المسئولون وهم أهل الذكر

sources.gloss: The Messenger of God is the reminder, and his household are the ones who will be questioned, and they are the people of the reminder.

essay.en:
God sends Moses to Pharaoh and his court bearing clear signs, and Moses announces, 'I am indeed an apostle of the Lord of all the worlds.' Tabatabai reads the whole episode as an answer to the Meccans, who had spurned the Prophet for not being one of the wealthy men they prized, so God set before them Pharaoh, who would weigh Moses against his own gold and kingdom [1]. When the signs came, the court only laughed. Each sign was greater than the one before, and God seized them with punishment - the flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood - that they might turn back [1][2].

Under each scourge they came to Moses calling him 'magician' and begging him to invoke his Lord by the covenant made with him, promising to be guided; but the moment relief came, they broke their pledge [2]. Tabrisi records that in their speech 'magician' named a learned man and was a title of honour, while Tabatabai holds it was said here in mockery [2][1].

Pharaoh then rallies his people, boasting of the kingdom of Egypt and the rivers of the Nile that run beneath him, and asking whether he is not better than a wretch who can barely speak. He demands why Moses was not given gold bracelets or escorted by angels - the marks, Tabrisi notes, by which that people ennobled a chief [2]. So he made light of his people's minds and they obeyed him, a transgressing lot [5]. When they roused God's wrath He drowned them all and made them forerunners into the Fire and a warning for those who came after [3].

Tusi and Tabrisi read the account as consolation for the Prophet: his people's mockery would end as Pharaoh's did, in the believer's ascendancy [4][2].

note.en: Pharaoh calls Moses 'a wretch who cannot even speak clearly,' mocking an impediment Moses had before his mission; Tabrisi notes God had lifted it, answering his plea, 'You have been granted your request, O Moses' (20:36) [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ولقد دخل موسى بن عمران ومعه اخوه هرون على فرعون وعليهما مدارع الصوف وبأيديهما العصا فشرطا له ان اسلم فلذلك بقاء ملكه ودوام عزّه فقال الا تعجبون من هذين يشرطان لي دوام العزّ وبقاء الملك وهما بما ترون من حال الفقر والذلّ فهلاّ القي عليهما اساور من ذهب

text.en: Moses son of Imran entered upon Pharaoh with his brother Aaron, both in coarse wool, staffs in hand, and pledged that if he submitted his kingdom and glory would endure. Pharaoh said, 'Do you not wonder at these two, guaranteeing me lasting power while in the poverty you see? Why were no gold bracelets thrown upon them?'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله عز و جل لا يأسف كأسفنا، و لكنه خلق أولياء لنفسه، يأسفون و يرضون، و هم مخلوقون مربوبون، فجعل رضاهم رضا نفسه، و سخطهم سخط نفسه، لأنه جعلهم الدعاة إليه، و الأدلاء عليه، فلذلك صاروا كذلك
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi, from his uncle Hamza ibn Bazi, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God does not grieve as we grieve. But He created friends for Himself who grieve and are pleased, and they are created and nurtured. He made their pleasure His pleasure and their displeasure His displeasure, because He made them those who call to Him and guide to Him; that is why they became so.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فرجّحوا الرجل على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بكثرة ماله مثّل لهم بقصة موسى عليه السلام وفرعون وقومه

sources.gloss: They preferred the wealthy man over the Prophet on account of his abundant wealth, so God set before them the story of Moses and Pharaoh and his people.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يعنون بذلك يا أيّها العالم وكان الساحر عندهم عظيماً يعظّمونه ولم يكن صفة ذمّ

sources.gloss: They meant by it 'O scholar'; the magician among them was a great one whom they revered, and it was not a term of blame.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: أي متقدّمين إلى النار … أي عبرة وموعظة

sources.gloss: Meaning forerunners to the Fire ... meaning a lesson and an admonition.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وإنما أخبر الله تعالى وقص خبر موسى وما جرى له تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله والمعنى إن حال موسى مع قومه وحالك مع قومك سواء

sources.gloss: God related the story of Moses only as a consolation for the Prophet; the meaning is that the case of Moses with his people and yours with your people are alike.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يعني فرعون استخف عقول قومه، فأطاعوه في ما دعاهم اليه، لانه احتج عليهم بما ليس بدليل

sources.gloss: Meaning Pharaoh made light of his people's intellects, and they obeyed him in what he called them to, because he argued against them with what is no proof.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن الله عز و جل لا يأسف كأسفنا، و لكنه خلق أولياء لنفسه، يأسفون و يرضون، و هم مخلوقون مربوبون، فجعل رضاهم رضا نفسه، و سخطهم سخط نفسه

sources.gloss: Indeed God, mighty and exalted, does not grieve as we grieve; but He created friends for Himself who grieve and are pleased, and they are created and nurtured; He made their pleasure His pleasure and their displeasure His displeasure.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ولقد دخل موسى بن عمران ومعه اخوه هرون على فرعون وعليهما مدارع الصوف … فهلاّ القي عليهما اساور من ذهب

sources.gloss: Moses son of Imran entered upon Pharaoh with his brother Aaron, both in coarse wool ... Why then were gold bracelets not thrown upon them?

essay.en:
The passage opens with the Son of Mary cited as an example, at which 'your people raise an outcry' (57). The commentators give more than one occasion for it. Tabatabai, reading this Meccan surah on its own terms and setting the narrations aside, takes the example to be God's own description of Jesus at the opening of Surah Maryam, the one Meccan surah that tells his story in full [1]. Tusi records instead that when God likened Jesus to Adam, created without a father, some of Quraysh objected, and that some report the Prophet likening Ali to Jesus, at which hypocrites protested [6]. The outcry itself, the lexicographers hold, is clamor and laughter [3].

Verse 58 gives their taunt, 'Are our gods better or he?' - which the commentators say they raised not to find the truth but for the sake of contention, and God names them a contentious lot [1][6]. The answer follows: Jesus 'was just a servant whom We had blessed' and made an exemplar for the Children of Israel, a man honored with prophethood, not a god (59) [1][6]. Verse 60 adds that had God willed, He could set angels on the earth as successors; Tabatabai reads this as removing the pagans' claim that such perfection belongs to angels alone [1], while Tabrisi reads it plainly of angels replacing mankind [3].

The passage then turns to the Hour. Tabatabai reads 'he is a portent of the Hour' (61) as Jesus himself, whose birth without a father and reviving of the dead show that resurrection is possible; others read it of his descent before the Hour [1][4]. The believer is told to follow the straight path and not let Satan, the manifest enemy, bar the way (62). Verses 63 to 65 recall Jesus' own mission: he brought wisdom and clear proofs and called his people to fear God and worship the one Lord, yet the factions differed among themselves, and woe was pronounced on the wrongdoers [4][7]. The passage closes by warning that the Hour may overtake them suddenly (66), and that on that day friends become one another's enemies, except the Godwary, whose friendship, formed for God, endures [2][8].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن فيك شبها من عيسى بن مريم، لو لا أن تقول فيك طوائف من امتي ما قالت النصارى في عيسى بن مريم، لقلت فيك قولا لا تمر بملإ من الناس إلا أخذوا التراب من تحت قدميك، يلتمسون بذلك البركة … فقالوا: ما رضي أن يضرب لابن عمه مثلا إلى عيسى بن مريم! فأنزل الله على نبيه
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The Messenger of God said to Ali: 'In you is a likeness of Jesus son of Mary. Were it not that groups of my community would say of you what the Christians said of Jesus, I would say words that would make people take dust from under your feet for blessing.' Quraysh grew angry, and the verse came down.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: مثلي في هذه الأمة مثل عيسى ابن مريم، أحبه قوم فغالوا في حبه فهلكوا، و أبغضه قوم فأفرطوا في بغضه فهلكوا، و اقتصد فيه قوم فنجوا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abdullah ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn Numayr, from Sharik, from Uthman ibn Umayr al-Bajali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ali

text.en: My likeness in this community is the likeness of Jesus son of Mary: a people loved him and went to excess in loving him and perished, a people hated him and went too far in hating him and perished, and a people kept to the middle course concerning him and were saved.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: عنى بذلك أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) … قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله): يا علي، أنت علم هذه الامة، فمن اتبعك نجا، و من تخلف عنك هلك و هوى
narrations.chain: narrated with the chain omitted, from Zurara ibn A'yan

text.en: I asked Abu Abdillah about the words 'Indeed he is a portent of the Hour.' He said, 'By that He meant the Commander of the Faithful,' and that the Messenger of God said, 'O Ali, you are the sign of this community; whoever follows you is saved, and whoever holds back from you perishes.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: سألت أبا جعفر (عليه السلام) عن قول الله عز و جل … هي ساعة القائم (عليه السلام)، تأتيهم بغتة
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas, from Ali ibn Abdillah ibn Asad, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Isma'il ibn Yasar, from Ali ibn Ja'far al-Hadrami, from Zurara ibn A'yan

text.en: I asked Abu Ja'far about the words 'Do they not consider that the Hour may overtake them suddenly?' He said, 'It is the hour of al-Qaim; it will come upon them suddenly.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ألا كل خلة كانت في الدنيا في غير الله فإنها تصير عداوة يوم القيامة

text.en: Every friendship formed in this world for other than God turns into enmity on the Day of Resurrection.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: يا أبا محمد … و الله ما أراد بهذا غيركم
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Abdillah, in the hadith of Abu Basir

text.en: O Abu Muhammad: 'On that day friends will be one another's enemies, except the Godwary' - by God, He meant none but you.

perspectives.en: The two traditions read the occasion differently. Tabari reports that when the Quran named idols as fuel of hell, the pagans objected that Christians worship Jesus and said they were content for their gods to share his lot [21]. Ibn Kathir records the same debate, sparked by Abdullah ibn al-Zibara, who argued that Jesus, Uzayr, and the angels are all worshipped, and the Quraysh thought he had won [27]. The Shia narrations instead place the verse at the Prophet's likening of Ali to Jesus son of Mary, at which his opponents took offense and mocked him [14].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: هو ما أنزله الله من وصفه في أول سورة مريم فإنها السورة المكية الوحيدة التي وردت فيها قصة عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام تفصيلاً

sources.gloss: What is meant is what God revealed of his description at the opening of Surah Maryam, the only Meccan surah in which the story of Jesus son of Mary came in detail.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وأما الأخلاء من المتقين فإن مخالتهم تتأكد وتنفعهم يومئذٍ

sources.gloss: As for the friends who are God-fearing, their friendship is strengthened and benefits them on that day.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: والمعنى لو نشاء أهلكناكم وجعلنا الملائكة بدلكم سكّان الأرض يعمرونها ويعبدون الله

sources.gloss: The meaning is: had We wished, We would have destroyed you and set the angels in your place as dwellers of the earth, populating it and worshipping God.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يعني أنّ نزول عيسى ع من أشراط الساعة يعلم بها قربها

sources.gloss: That is, the descent of Jesus is among the portents of the Hour, by which its nearness is known.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: لولا أني اخاف ان يقال فيك ما قالت النصارى في عيسى لقلت فيك قولا لا تمرّ بملاء إلا اخذوا التراب من تحت قدميك

sources.gloss: It is related that the Prophet said to Ali: 'Were I not afraid that of you would be said what the Christians said of Jesus, I would say words about you such that you would pass by no gathering but they took the dust from under your feet.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وقال قتادة: يعني الفرق الذين تحزبوا فى أمر عيسى عليه السلام

sources.gloss: Qatada said: the factions means the groups that formed parties over the matter of Jesus.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: يعني من كانت خلته فى دار الدنيا فى غير طاعة الله بل كانت في معصية الله، فان تلك الخلة تنقلب عليه عداوة

sources.gloss: That is, whoever's friendship in this world was in other than obedience to God, indeed in disobedience to God, that friendship turns into enmity against him.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: ألا كل خلة كانت في الدنيا في غير الله فإنها تصير عداوة يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: al-Sadiq said: every friendship in this world for other than God becomes enmity on the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن فيك شبها من عيسى بن مريم، لو لا أن تقول فيك طوائف من امتي ما قالت النصارى في عيسى بن مريم، لقلت فيك قولا لا تمر بملإ من الناس إلا أخذوا التراب من تحت قدميك، يلتمسون بذلك البركة

sources.gloss: In you is a likeness of Jesus son of Mary. Were it not that groups of my community would say of you what the Christians said of Jesus son of Mary, I would say words about you such that you would pass by no gathering but they took the dust from under your feet, seeking blessing by it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: عنى بذلك أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام)

sources.gloss: By that He meant the Commander of the Faithful.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هي ساعة القائم (عليه السلام)، تأتيهم بغتة

sources.gloss: It is the hour of al-Qaim; it will come upon them suddenly.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و الله ما أراد بهذا غيركم

sources.gloss: By God, He meant none but you by this.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: قد رضينا بأن تكون آلهتنا مع عيسى وعُزَير والملائكة

sources.gloss: The polytheists said: we are content for our gods to be with Jesus, Uzayr, and the angels.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: سلوا محمداً أكل ما يعبد من دون الله في جهنم مع من عبده؟

sources.gloss: Ask Muhammad: is everything worshipped besides God in Hell along with those who worshipped it?

essay.en:
Sura al-Zukhruf ends by placing the two outcomes of the resurrection side by side. God calls to the God-fearing, 'O My servants! Today you will have no fear, nor will you grieve.' Al-Mizan reads this as spoken on the Day itself, securing them against every evil at once, the feared and the certain alike [1]. These servants are those who believed in Our signs and submitted to God's will [1]. They enter paradise with their spouses, whom al-Mizan takes to be their believing wives in this world, since the maidens of paradise never leave it [1]. Golden dishes and goblets circle among them, with whatever the souls desire and eyes delight in - words, Majma notes, that no gathering of all creatures could better in describing paradise's bounty [3]. Against this, the guilty abide in hell; al-Mizan hears 'the guilty' as wider than the disbelievers, everyone steeped in crime [1]. They beg Malik, the keeper of the fire, to let their Lord finish them off, and are told they will stay on [1].

The sura then turns to the Meccans who reject the Prophet. 'Have they settled on some plan? Indeed, We too are settling' answers, al-Mizan explains, their plotting against Muhammad with God's counter-plotting, while the recording angels note even their secret talk [2]. The Prophet is told to say that, were the All-beneficent to have offspring, he would be the first to worship; the conditional wording, al-Mizan observes, denies the son by denying he exists at all [2]. God is glorified, and the Prophet is told to leave them to their play until the promised day - a threat, al-Tibyan says, of the punishment to come [9]. He is God in the sky and God on the earth, which means, al-Mizan stresses, that His godhood reaches both realms, not that He is contained in either [2]. Those invoked besides Him hold no power to intercede, except whoever witnesses to the truth on knowledge [2]. Asked who created them, the deniers say 'Allah,' yet turn away. The sura closes with the Prophet's plaint, 'these are a people who will not have faith,' and God's answer: disregard them, say 'Peace,' soon they will know.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sajjad
narrations.arabic: إذا كان يوم القيامة نادى منادٍ لا خوف عليكم اليوم ولا أنتم تحزنون فإذا قالها لم يبق أحدٌ إلا رفع رأسه فإذا قال الذين آمنوا بآياتنا وكانوا مسلمين لم يبق أحدٌ إلا طأطأ رأسه إلا المسلمين المحبين … هذه فاطمة بنت محمد تمر بكم هي ومن معها إلى الجنة
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Zakariyya al-Dihqan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Siraj, from Abu Hafs, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: On the Day of Resurrection a caller cries, 'No fear is upon you today, nor will you grieve,' and every head lifts. When he says, 'those who believed in Our signs and had been Muslims,' every head drops but the believing lovers. Then it is called: This is Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, passing to paradise with those with her.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الرجل في الجنة يبقى على مائدته أيام الدنيا ويأكل في أكلة واحدة بمقدار ما أكله في الدنيا
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The man in paradise stays at his table for the length of the world's days, and in a single meal eats the measure of all he ate in the world.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: حَيْثُ كَتَبُوا الْكِتَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَ تَعَاهَدُوا وَ تَوَافَقُوا لَئِنْ مَضَى مُحَمَّدٌ لَا تَكُونُ الْخِلَافَةُ فِي بَنِي هَاشِمٍ وَ لَا النُّبُوَّةُ أَبَداً فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِيهِمْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ … وَ هَاتَانِ الْآيَتَانِ نَزَلَتَا فِيهِمْ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ
narrations.chain: from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: They wrote a pact among themselves and agreed that, once Muhammad passed away, the caliphate would never rest in the clan of Hashim, nor prophethood. God, said the Imam, sent down these two verses about them on that day: 'Have they settled on some plan? Indeed, We too are settling.'

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين أي الجاحدين، التأويل في هذا القول باطنه مضاد لظاهره

text.en: 'If the All-beneficent had offspring, I would be the first to worship' - that is, the first of the deniers. In this saying, the Imam said, the inner sense runs opposite to its outward wording.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هذا كلام زنديق خبيث، إذا رجعت إليه فقل له: ما أسمك بالكوفة؟ فإنه يقول: فلان، فقل له: ما اسمك بالبصرة؟ … كذلك الله ربنا في السماء إله، و في البحار إله، و في الأرض إله، و في القفار إله، و في كل مكان إله
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam

text.en: A dualist claimed this verse backed his belief in two gods. The Imam called it foul heresy and said: ask his name in Kufa, then in Basra. As one man has one name in each place, so God is God in the sky, God in the seas, God on the earth, and God in every place.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Jawad
narrations.arabic: سألت أبا جعفر الثاني عليه السلام ما معنى الواحد فقال إجماع الألسن عليه بالوحدانية كقوله تعالى ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Abu Hashim al-Jafari

text.en: I asked Abu Jafar the Second what 'the One' means. He said: the agreement of all tongues upon His oneness, as in His words, 'If you ask them who created them, they will surely say, Allah.'

perspectives.en: On verses 78 to 80 the two traditions aim the same words at different targets. Tabari reads 'We certainly brought you the truth' as the message God sent Quraysh through Muhammad [40], and Qurtubi passes on Muqatil's report that 'Have they settled on some plan?' was the idolaters' scheme in the assembly house to kill the Prophet [59]. The Shia narrations gloss 'the truth' as the guardianship of Ali [24] and read the plan as a written pact sworn in the Kaaba to keep leadership from the Prophet's household [25]. Both hold that the recording angels miss nothing of what is hidden.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: وفي الخطاب تأمين لهم من كل مكروه محتمل أو مقطوع به

sources.gloss: In this address is reassurance for them against every evil, whether merely possible or altogether certain.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بل أحكموا أمراً من الكيد بك يا محمد فإنا محكمون الكيد بهم

sources.gloss: Rather, they have contrived a plot against you, Muhammad, and We are contriving Our plot against them.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وقد جمع الله سبحانه بقوله ما تشتهي الأنفس وتلذّ الأعين ما لو اجتمع الخلائق كلهم على أن يصفوا ما في الجنة من أنواع النعيم لم يزيدوا على ما انتظمته هاتان الصفتان

sources.gloss: In the words 'whatever the souls desire and eyes delight in,' God has gathered so much that were all creatures to join in describing the bounties of paradise, they could add nothing beyond what these two phrases hold.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: ثم قال لنبيه صلى الله عليه وآله على وجه التهديد للكفار فذرهم أي اتركهم يخوضوا فى الباطل ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون

sources.gloss: He said to His Prophet, by way of threatening the disbelievers: leave them to plunge into falsehood and play until they meet their day, the day they are promised.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: إن الرجل في الجنة يبقى على مائدته أيام الدنيا ويأكل في أكلة واحدة بمقدار ما أكله في الدنيا

sources.gloss: The man in paradise stays at his table for the length of the world's days, and eats in a single meal the measure of all he ate in the world.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: لقد جئناكم بالحق يعني بولاية أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام ولكن أكثركم للحق كارهون يعني لولاية أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

sources.gloss: 'We certainly brought you the truth' means the guardianship of the Commander of the Believers, and 'most of you were averse to the truth' means averse to his guardianship.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ثم ذكر على إثر هذا خبرهم، و ما تعاهدوا عليه في الكعبة، أن لا يردوا الأمر في أهل بيت رسول الله

sources.gloss: Then it mentions their affair and what they pledged one another in the Kaaba: not to return the leadership to the household of God's Messenger.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين أي الجاحدين، التأويل في هذا القول باطنه مضاد لظاهره

sources.gloss: 'If the All-beneficent had offspring, I would be the first to worship' - that is, the first of the deniers; in this saying the inner meaning is the opposite of its outward wording.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هذا كلام زنديق خبيث … كذلك الله ربنا في السماء إله، و في البحار إله، و في الأرض إله، و في القفار إله، و في كل مكان إله

sources.gloss: This is the talk of a foul heretic ... likewise God our Lord: in the sky God, in the seas God, on the earth God, in the wastes God, and in every place God.

sources.author: Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi

excerpt.text: إذا كان يوم القيامة نادى منادٍ لا خوف عليكم اليوم ولا أنتم تحزنون … هذه فاطمة بنت محمد تمر بكم هي ومن معها إلى الجنة

sources.gloss: On the Day of Resurrection a caller cries, 'No fear is upon you today, nor will you grieve' ... This is Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, passing by you with those with her to paradise.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: لقد جئناكم بالحق يقول: لقد أرسلنا إليكم يا معشر قريش رسولنا محمدا بالحق

sources.gloss: 'We certainly brought you the truth' means: We sent to you, O company of Quraysh, Our messenger Muhammad with the truth.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: قال مقاتل: نزلت في تدبيرهم المكر بالنبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم في دار الندوة، حين استقر أمرهم على ما أشار به أبو جهل عليهم أن يبرز من كل قبيلة رجل ليشتركوا في قتله

sources.gloss: Muqatil said it was revealed about their plotting against the Prophet in the assembly house, when they settled on Abu Jahl's proposal that one man from each tribe take part in killing him.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: حَيْثُ كَتَبُوا الْكِتَابَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَ تَعَاهَدُوا وَ تَوَافَقُوا لَئِنْ مَضَى مُحَمَّدٌ لَا تَكُونُ الْخِلَافَةُ فِي بَنِي هَاشِمٍ وَ لَا النُّبُوَّةُ أَبَداً … وَ هَاتَانِ الْآيَتَانِ نَزَلَتَا فِيهِمْ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ

sources.gloss: When they wrote the pact among themselves and agreed that, should Muhammad pass away, the caliphate would never be in the clan of Hashim, nor prophethood ... and these two verses were revealed about them on that day.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: سألت أبا جعفر الثاني عليه السلام ما معنى الواحد فقال إجماع الألسن عليه بالوحدانية كقوله تعالى ولئن سألتهم من خلقهم ليقولن الله

sources.gloss: I asked Abu Jafar the Second what 'the One' means. He said: the agreement of all tongues upon His oneness, as in His words, 'If you ask them who created them, they will surely say, Allah.'
